query: For an AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy in its uniform, fine lamellar state, whose strength and plasticity remain below industrial application requirements, what single intervention could improve performance for fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive conditions? State the proposed intervention, mechanism, predicted outcome relative to the starting alloy, applicable operating and test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit falsification criteria.

generation.hypothesis: A controlled thermomechanical post‐processing treatment—specifically, moderate cold rolling (≈8% reduction) immediately followed by low‐temperature annealing—will refine the eutectic lamellar microstructure of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 high‐entropy alloy, thereby enhancing its strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion stability under extreme service conditions for fasteners.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast, uniform fine lamellar (fcc/B2) eutectic microstructure with performance below industrial fastener requirements
generation.intervention: Apply a thermomechanical treatment consisting of moderate cold rolling (≈8% reduction) followed immediately by a controlled low‐temperature annealing step
generation.conditions: Service environments featuring cyclic temperature fluctuations (from room temperature up to about 700°C), long-term mechanical loading that induces room-temperature creep, and exposure to corrosive media (e.g., salt-containing solutions)
generation.structural_mediator: A refined duplex lamellar microstructure characterized by a reduced lamellar spacing, increased dislocation density, and more stabilized/coherent phase boundaries
generation.mechanism: Cold rolling introduces beneficial strain and increases dislocation density while refining lamellar spacing; subsequent low-temperature annealing allows controlled recovery and partial recrystallization, which together enhance strain hardening and stabilize interfaces against creep and corrosion
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the untreated alloy, the treated alloy is expected to exhibit higher yield and tensile strengths and improved ductility, accompanied by reduced room-temperature creep rates and enhanced resistance to corrosive attack
generation.baseline: The as-cast uniform fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy with mechanical properties that fall short of industrial requirements for fasteners
generation.boundary: The improvements are anticipated when processing parameters are carefully optimized and the enhanced properties are maintained under service conditions up to approximately 700°C and typical corrosive exposures; performance outside these limits remains uncertain
generation.uncertainty: While directional improvements are expected, the exact magnitude of the strength, ductility, and creep/corrosion enhancements depends on the precise tuning of processing parameters and needs further empirical quantification

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 samples: one set will remain in the as-cast state and the other will undergo the proposed moderate cold rolling (≈8% reduction) followed by low-temperature annealing. Subject both sets to identical testing conditions that simulate cyclic thermal fluctuations (up to ~700°C), long-duration creep at room temperature, and corrosion tests in a salt (e.g., NaCl) solution.
measurements: Yield and tensile strength (via standardized tensile testing)
Elongation/dialectility (via tensile testing)
Creep rate under a constant load at room temperature
Corrosion rate and electrochemical parameters (e.g., corrosion current density and potential)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples fail to show statistically significant improvements (for example, less than approximately a 10–15% increase in both strength and ductility, no measurable reduction in creep rate, or no improvement in corrosion performance) compared to the as-cast controls under identical test conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: These results showed that the yield strength (1437 ± 26 MPa), tensile strength (1562 ± 33 MPa), and elongation (14 ± 1%) of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy after annealing at low temperature were significantly improved compared with the as-cast alloy. Eutectic high-entropy alloys exhibit an excellent balance of toughness and strength at room temperature. However, there is still an immediate requirement to design structural components with more strength and ductility due to the increasing technical requirements and harsher operating environments in industrial applications. The demand for stronger and more ductile structural elements has increased as airplane components have become more demanding and technical standards have advanced. Therefore, it is of significance to develop a new eutectic high-entropy alloy with superior properties based on AlCoCrFeNi2.1.

The eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, with an fcc/B2 dual-phase constitution and a uniform and fine lamellar microstructure, exhibited the combination of both high fracture strength and high ductility, which has never been achieved in previously reported HEAs. The room temperature tensile test showed a fracture stress of 944 MPa and an elongation of 25.6%, from the engineering stress-strain curve given in Fig. 4a. These values converted to 1186 MPa and 22.8% in the true stress/strain condition. Noteworthily, this alloy exhibited an ultra-high strain hardening behavior, having the proof stress (the proof stress is determined by shifting the linear elastic curve to 0.2% strain. We choose to not to call it the yield stress, as the mechanism for such a low elastic limit is still unclear at this stage.) of 75 MPa but reaching the fracture stress close to 1.2 GPa. At elevated temperatures of 600 and 700°C (Fig. 4b), the proof stress, fracture stress and elongation were 95 MPa, 806 MPa, 33.7%, and 108 MPa, 538 MPa, 22.9%, respectively, both in the true stress/strain condition. In this work, we successfully achieve a superior strength–ductility combination in AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEAs by introducing two concurrent effects, the two-hierarchical constraint effect and the self-generated microcrack-arresting mechanisms. The underlying origin lying behind the observed mechanical response is the inherited lamellar geometry from the as-cast EHEA. It is known that grain refinement to the nano/ultrafine-grained regime can render material stronger, but this process is usually accompanied by a dramatic loss of ductility. However, with a composite lamellar architecture, the ultrafine-grained duplex microstructure in this study achieves an improved strength–ductility synergy. Phase decomposition is applied to optimize properties instead of just being a phase-instability phenomenon frequently observed in single-phase HEAs, which may encourage further research in this area. In addition, the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA could be simply processed to achieve properties that are an improvement over traditional TRIP (transformation-induced plasticity) and TWIP (twinning-induced plasticity) steels (Fig. 5). drafts.hypothesis: A tailored aging heat treatment that induces a uniform dispersion of nano‐scale coherent precipitates in the eutectic high-entropy alloy will improve its strength, creep resistance, and corrosion resistance without sacrificing ductility.
drafts.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 in a uniform, fine lamellar eutectic microstructure with performance below industrial application requirements.
drafts.intervention: Subject the alloy to an optimized aging heat treatment (e.g., holding at an intermediate temperature around 700–800°C for a controlled duration) to precipitate nano‐scale, coherent secondary phases within the lamellar matrix.
drafts.conditions: The intervention is intended for fasteners that experience extreme temperature fluctuations (up to ~800°C), long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosive service environments. Laboratory tests should mimic accelerated thermal cycling, prolonged creep exposure, and corrosive conditions.
drafts.structural_mediator: Uniformly distributed nano-scale precipitates that form within the lamellar matrix as a result of the aging treatment.
drafts.mechanism: The nano-scale precipitates act as obstacles to dislocation motion, thereby increasing yield strength and reducing creep deformation. In addition, their presence helps stabilize the microstructure during thermal cycling and minimizes localized galvanic cells at phase boundaries, thus enhancing corrosion resistance.
drafts.predicted_outcome: Compared to the untreated alloy, the aged alloy is predicted to exhibit a measurable increase in yield strength and improved resistance to creep and corrosion, while retaining sufficient plasticity for application.
drafts.baseline: Performance metrics (mechanical properties and corrosion resistance) of the as-cast uniform fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy.
drafts.boundary: The beneficial effects are expected to operate only within temperature regimes where the nano-scale precipitates remain stable (e.g., below temperatures that cause precipitate coarsening or dissolution) and under the specific load and corrosive conditions used during testing.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples: one set receives the proposed aging heat treatment and the other is retained as the control. Subject both sets to accelerated thermal cycling, long-term creep testing at room temperature, and standardized corrosion tests. Use transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) to assess the formation and distribution of nano-scale precipitates.
measurements: Yield strength from tensile tests
Ductility/plasticity (e.g., elongation at break)
Creep rate under constant load at room temperature
Corrosion rate in simulated service environments
Microstructural parameters (precipitate size, volume fraction, and distribution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the heat-treated samples do not show statistically significant improvements in yield strength, creep resistance, and corrosion performance compared to the control, or if microstructural analysis fails to reveal the predicted nano-scale precipitates, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: A subcritical aging treatment will promote the precipitation of nano-scale, ordered B2 phases along the lamellar interfaces in the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, thereby enhancing its strength, creep resistance, and corrosion stability under extreme service conditions.
drafts.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with performance below current industrial application requirements.
drafts.intervention: A controlled subcritical aging heat treatment (for example, holding the alloy at approximately 700°C for 30 to 60 minutes) applied after solidification.
drafts.conditions: Fasteners exposed to extreme temperature fluctuations (e.g. -40°C to 300°C), long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep environments, and corrosive media.
drafts.structural_mediator: Nano-scale B2 precipitates forming particularly at or near the lamellar interfaces.
drafts.mechanism: The subcritical aging treatment induces precipitation hardening: the fine, ordered B2 phases impede dislocation motion and reduce grain boundary sliding, resulting in increased yield strength and creep resistance. Furthermore, their presence may limit the migration of corrosive species along vulnerable interfaces, thus enhancing corrosion resistance.
drafts.predicted_outcome: Relative to the starting uniform fine lamellar state, the alloy will exhibit a statistically significant increase in yield strength, improved resistance to room-temperature creep under long-term load, and enhanced corrosion resistance under cyclic extremes.
drafts.baseline: The as-cast or rapidly cooled uniform fine lamellar microstructure which, while eutectic, does not meet the required performance specifications for extreme environments.
drafts.boundary: The intervention is applicable under the test conditions of thermal cycling between approximately -40°C and 300°C, continuous and cyclic mechanical loads that simulate industrial fastener performance over extended periods, and corrosive environments representative of service conditions. Results must be validated through standardized tensile, creep, and corrosion tests.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy samples: one set to receive the proposed aging treatment and one control set maintained in the as-cast state. Subject both sets to a battery of mechanical tests (tensile tests for yield strength, long-duration creep tests), thermal cycling between -40°C and 300°C, and standardized corrosion evaluations (e.g., potentiodynamic polarization). Complement these tests with microstructural analyses (e.g., TEM/SEM) to verify the formation, size, and distribution of B2 precipitates.
measurements: Yield strength and ultimate tensile strength
Creep rate and rupture life under constant load
Corrosion current density and potential
Microstructural evidence of nano-scale precipitate formation (size, distribution, and phase identity)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermally aged samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in mechanical strength, creep resistance, and corrosion performance compared to the control, or if microstructural analysis fails to show the anticipated nano-scale B2 precipitates (or shows deleterious phases formation), the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: A controlled thermomechanical treatment—specifically, a moderate cold deformation (≈8% cold rolling) immediately followed by an optimized low‐temperature annealing—will refine the internal lamellar structure of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, leading to simultaneous improvements in strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion performance under extreme service conditions.
drafts.material_initial_state: AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy in its as‐cast, uniform, fine lamellar (fcc/B2) state with mechanical properties below industrial requirements.
drafts.intervention: Apply a single-step intervention consisting of a moderate plastic deformation (≈8% cold rolling) followed by a low-temperature annealing treatment.
drafts.conditions: Designed for fastener applications operating under extreme temperature fluctuations (from ambient up to ~700°C), long-term mechanical loading including room-temperature creep, and corrosive environments (e.g., salt-containing media).
drafts.structural_mediator: A refined duplex microstructure in which the lamellar (fcc/B2) architecture is maintained but further subdivided and strengthened by increased dislocation densities and controlled submicron scale precipitates at the phase boundaries.
drafts.mechanism: The cold rolling introduces beneficial strain and increases dislocation density while slightly refining the lamellar spacing. Subsequent low-temperature annealing allows for recovery and subtle recrystallization without coarsening the lamellae. This combination enhances dislocation pinning and enables self-arresting mechanisms at microcrack sites, which collectively bolster yield and fracture strength, reduce creep rates, and improve corrosion resistance by stabilizing low-energy phase boundaries.
drafts.predicted_outcome: Compared to the untreated alloy, the treated alloy is predicted to exhibit significantly higher proof and fracture stresses (with an anticipated increase in true yield/fracture strength by at least 15% or more), improved ductility, reduced room-temperature creep rates, and enhanced resistance to corrosive attack.
drafts.baseline: The untreated AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy shows a room temperature proof stress of ~75 MPa and a fracture stress nearing 1.2 GPa, with ductility and creep resistance that do not meet demanding industrial fastener requirements.
drafts.boundary: The anticipated performance improvements are expected to be maintained in service environments from room temperature to about 700°C. The effectiveness of this treatment may be limited outside these temperature ranges or under conditions where excessive deformation rates are encountered.

Test both sets under identical mechanical (tensile and creep at room temperature and up to 700°C) and corrosion conditions (e.g., immersion in 3.5% NaCl solution).
measurements: Proof stress / yield strength (via tensile testing)
Fracture stress and elongation (tensile testing)
Creep rate (under controlled loading at room temperature and elevated temperatures)
Corrosion current density and corrosion potential (electrochemical tests in NaCl solution)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the thermomechanically treated samples do not show statistically significant improvements (at least a 15% increase in yield and fracture strength, measurable reduction in creep rate, and no deterioration in electrochemical corrosion parameters relative to the control), then the hypothesis is falsified.

drafts.hypothesis: A controlled thermomechanical post‐processing treatment consisting of moderate cold rolling (around an 8% reduction) followed by low‐temperature annealing will refine the lamellar microstructure of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy and simultaneously enhance its strength, ductility, creep resistance, and corrosion durability for fastener applications in extreme service environments.
drafts.material_initial_state: Uniform, fine lamellar dual-phase (fcc/B2) eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 high-entropy alloy in the as-cast condition
drafts.intervention: Apply a tailored thermomechanical treatment—specifically, moderate cold rolling (~8% thickness reduction) followed by controlled low-temperature annealing
drafts.conditions: Service conditions involving cyclic extreme temperature fluctuations (up to about 700°C), long-term mechanical loading that may induce room-temperature creep, and exposure to corrosive environments (e.g., NaCl-containing media)
drafts.structural_mediator: A refined ultrafine-grained duplex lamellar structure with more coherent phase boundaries and reduced defect density
drafts.mechanism: Cold rolling increases dislocation density and reduces lamellar spacing, while subsequent low-temperature annealing promotes partial recrystallization that optimizes the phase distribution. This dual effect enhances strain hardening (via a two-hierarchical constraint effect) and stabilizes the microstructure against creep and corrosion by creating low-energy phase boundaries.
drafts.predicted_outcome: An increase in both yield and tensile strengths with maintained or improved ductility, accompanied by reduced room-temperature creep rates and improved resistance to corrosion relative to the as-cast state
drafts.baseline: As-cast uniform thin-lamella AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy with moderate strength and ductility that do not meet industrial fastener requirements
drafts.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective when processing parameters are optimized to avoid excessive grain growth and phase coarsening, and when used under conditions not exceeding the tested temperature range (up to approximately 700°C) and corrosive exposures typical of industrial fastener environments

Perform a series of tests under simulated service conditions that include cyclic temperature variations (up to ~700°C), constant load creep testing at room temperature, and corrosion testing in a NaCl-containing solution.
